chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Cab's band lacked Chick's spirit
summary: The band was well drilled but Cab was a showman, so McRae told the men he came from the big tent.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

Well that's partly because also the nature of the gigs that Cab Calloway played -- that he was more of a showman.

He was more of a showman and the band didn't have -- really too much to do. And the funny thing, when he turned us loose on an instrumental, you know, it was just like, what's happening here, ain't nothing. You know, like, it's just one of them -- it's always in the (inaudible) Cab Calloway (inaudible). Now if you played an instrument with Chick, you'd be jumping, you know what I mean? But Cab always get off in his tempo. Everything had to be in his tempo, you know.
What would you tell the guys when you went in to Cab's band?
Oh, I told them, I say, "I came from the big tent." They say, "What do you mean the big tent." I say, "Like Barnum and Bailey. Chick's like the greatest show on earth." You know, like --

which it was. You come out of Chick's band and go into some other band, you know, you look around and say, man, what's happening over here, you know. I'll tell you one thing. One of the times when I joined Chick Webb's band, the guy used to want to go work. You ever see musicians come to work -- you didn't have to (Inaudible) beg those guys to come in. They come to work -- when you get there, everybody be on the bandstand. One night I come in, everybody sitting up on the bandstand like fifteen minutes (Inaudible) ready. Chick sat over in the corner. Everybody was up on the bandstand. When Chick walk up on the bandstand, all the men are up there, you know what I mean? That's the same way with Cab's band, but the tempo and the atmosphere is different with Cab, you know. But we finally turned it around, because
